extracted.intended_audience: potential grantees, partners, policymakers, and the general public interested in Gates Foundation funding priorities
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation’s strategic criteria for selecting, funding, and partnering on development and public‑health work — emphasizing transformative, catalytic, equity‑focused investments across several target domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable transformative change (not incremental improvements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our role is to enable transformative change—not just incremental improvements—by taking risks others can’t or won’t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation seeks interventions that have the potential to radically improve outcomes rather than small, marginal gains. This is tied to a willingness to accept higher risk where others (e.g., governments, markets) will not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus where we can have the greatest impact on reducing inequities
rubrics_metrics.description: That means focusing on issues where we can have the greatest impact on reducing inequities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize problems and geographies where catalytic philanthropic investment can close gaps in health, opportunity, and services for those left behind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take risks to support bold ideas and approaches that show real promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Our funding is small compared to what governments spend, but we can take risks to support bold ideas and approaches that show real promise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation uses its relative flexibility to fund novel approaches and early‑stage innovations that may be too risky for other funders; examples include postpartum hemorrhage drapes and portable prenatal risk detectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop long‑term strategies that target catalytic impact
rubrics_metrics.description: We focus on developing long-term strategies that take on critical domestic US and global issues where we believe we can have the greatest catalytic impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for sustained, strategic engagements aimed at system change rather than one‑off short projects; emphasis on scalability and durable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and support people who could create better or more affordable solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask: Who, given the right support, could create better or more affordable solutions? We then help connect them with resources and partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors teams or individuals with potential to produce cost‑effective, improved solutions; Foundation provides networking, financing, and partnership facilitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner with governments, researchers, local leaders, and community changemakers
rubrics_metrics.description: We also bring together governments, researchers, local leaders, and community changemakers to share knowledge, collaborate, and align on shared goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on multi‑stakeholder collaboration and alignment to accelerate adoption and scale; partnerships should enable shared goals and knowledge exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work centers on specific priority areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work centers on health, gender equality, agriculture, nutrition, and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects outside these domains are less central to the Foundation’s core strategy; within these domains, the Foundation seeks interventions aligned with its equity and catalytic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support innovations that are affordable, scalable, and life‑changing
rubrics_metrics.description: These ideas often grow into innovations that can change lives—like postpartum hemorrhage drapes, portable devices that detect health risks during pregnancy, and waterless toilets that treat waste safely and affordably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for technologies and protocols that are low‑cost, scalable in low‑resource settings, and demonstrably improve health or livelihoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target high‑impact outcomes such as disease elimination and maternal/child health
rubrics_metrics.description: With our partners around the world, we work to eliminate infectious diseases, ensure the health of mothers and babies, and expand economic opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects aligned with major outcome goals (e.g., disease eradication, improved maternal/child survival, economic opportunity expansion) are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage and support local communities and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: We proudly partner with experts, local communities, and institutions across the world that are relentlessly supporting human potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should involve and empower local actors and institutions rather than impose external solutions; local engagement is a criterion for effectiveness and sustainability.
